Hi! I run a monthly tech meetup, about 80 people in the room. I want a live poll app I can run from my laptop and project on the screen, while everybody votes from their phone. Here is the whole thing I want, all at once:

1) HOST MODE: I create a question with 2-4 options, and I press Open voting. There should be a big obvious code or link my audience can type to get to the vote.
2) AUDIENCE MODE: someone on their phone opens it, types their name, picks an option, hits Vote. ONE VOTE PER PERSON — I don't want one guy voting five times for his favourite framework.
3) LIVE RESULTS: a bar chart of the options, with vote counts and percentages, that updates by itself on everybody's screen as votes come in. I must not have to refresh. This is the part I care about most — I want it updating while I'm standing there talking.
4) CLOSE VOTING: I close it, and the final result stays on screen with a 'Closed' state, and phones stop being able to vote.
5) HISTORY: later questions in the same evening, and I can go back and see the results of earlier questions. So questions are a list, one is 'open' at a time.

Also please tell me, in plain words, how the live updating actually works here — is it websockets, polling, what? I know some JS/React but I don't want hand-waving. And I'll be demoing this live on stage, so it has to not break.

    3  A live-audience poll for a meetup: the host (a laptop on the projector)
    4  creates a question with 2-4 options and opens voting; the audience (phones)
    5  votes once each; every screen shows the same live bar chart, which updates

    8  
    9  ## Running an evening
   10  
   11  1. Open the app on the laptop and choose "I'm the host" (route #/host).
   12  2. Type a question and 2-4 options, press "Add question", then "Open voting".
   13  3. The big link on the host screen is what the audience opens on their phone (it ends in #/vote).
   14  4. Talk. The chart moves on its own - on the projector and on every phone.
   15  5. Press "Close voting"; the final result stays on every screen. Earlier
   16     questions appear under "Earlier questions" with their final charts.
   17  
   18  ## Rehearsing on one laptop
   19  
   20  The host screen has a "Rehearsal" box while a question is open: type a
   21  made-up name, press "+1 <option>", and you have cast a vote as that
   22  person - be as many people as you like, from the one browser. The server
   23  action behind it requires the host's own permission, so no audience phone
   24  can ever reach it, and rehearsal votes obey the same one-per-name rule as
   25  real ones. They are stored under a "test:<name>" identity, flagged on the
   26  host screen ("N rehearsal votes in the counts"), and "Clear rehearsal
   27  votes" wipes every one of them from every question with a single press.
   28  Press it before the real show.
   29  
   30  ## How the live updating works
   31  
   32  No polling, nothing to refresh. Every open page keeps a live connection to
   33  the server. When anything changes (a vote, opening, closing), actor.ts
   34  emits a moment on the "poll" room topic (room.emit('poll', {})), and the
   35  server pushes it to every page subscribed to that topic (room.on('poll', ...)
   36  in main.ts). Each page then calls the "state" action once and re-renders.
   37  A vote therefore lands on every screen with one push plus one read.
   38  
   39  If the venue wifi blips and a page's live connection dies silently, that
   40  page still catches up: it refetches the moment the phone reports it is back
   41  online, whenever the page comes back to the foreground, and at worst 10
   42  seconds later while someone is actually looking at it. Hidden phones stay
   43  quiet, so 80 of them never turn into a request storm.
   44  
   45  ## One vote per person
   46  
   47  Two locks, both enforced on the server, never on the phone:
   48  
   49  1. The votes table's primary key is (question_id, visitor_id): the same
   50     browser can never hold two rows for the same question. The identity is
   51     the server's visitor id (a cookie), so a second tab, a refresh or a
   52     cleared cache on the same phone still counts once.
   53  2. One vote per name per question (a unique index on
